data.note: Perimeter divided into 32 door-padas of 11.25° each, clockwise. Pada 0 begins at 337.5°, the start of the North octant, so each compass octant holds four whole padas and a pada's quadrant is the octant direction/zone-from-bearing gives every bearing inside it. The devata names run in the Brihat Samhita 53.43-45 perimeter order, each side read clockwise from its corner, with Agni (the NE corner square) beginning at 45°; the same ring is served by entrance/pada and entrance/recommend. The 32-pada entrance grid, its bearings and its per-pada grades are later Vastu tradition, NOT a classical verse. Each pada labels its deity name and its quadrant separately: classical only where Brihat Samhita 53.43-48 (Iyer 1884, PD) names that devata and seats it on a perimeter square in that quadrant. The genuine verse-backed door rule is the 9-pada-per-side scheme of Manasara 38, surfaced below as classicalDoorScheme.

data.variantNote: 3 plan(s) generated and ranked by a weighted score of Vastu compliance (50%), usability (25%) and space efficiency (25%). The top-level rooms / mandala / compliance / svg are the recommended variant — "usability-first". Identical layouts are returned once, so fewer than the requested number can come back. Drawings are included unless "includeSvg": false; with drawings enabled, send "variantSvg": true to render every option (adds roughly 20 KB each). The 9-zone `mandala` is plot geometry and is identical for every variant, so it is returned once at the top level. When every option scores the SAME Vastu compliance, the classical (vastu-first) plan is recommended regardless of the other two axes.

data.variantNote: 3 plan(s) generated and ranked by a weighted score of Vastu compliance (50%), usability (25%) and space efficiency (25%). The top-level rooms / mandala / compliance / svg are the recommended variant — "usability-first". Identical layouts are returned once, so fewer than the requested number can come back. Drawings are included unless "includeSvg": false; with drawings enabled, send "variantSvg": true to render every option (adds roughly 20 KB each). The 9-zone `mandala` is plot geometry and is identical for every variant, so it is returned once at the top level. When every option scores the SAME Vastu compliance, the classical (vastu-first) plan is recommended regardless of the other two axes.

areaFit.basis: Mean of each room's areaFitPct. Living rooms under 75% of their request and service rooms (toilet, pooja, store, staircase, utility, balcony, lift, parking) over 1.5x are named. Scored apart from the placement index, which judges zones only.
areaFit.summary: Area fit 98/100: every living room has at least 75% of its requested area and no service room is over 1.5x its request.

compliance.indexBasis: proprietary Vedika compliance index — the same weighted placement index every Vastu score endpoint returns (room and zone weights, defects subtract); not a classical score
compliance.note: All 9 rooms placed in target/acceptable zones. Brahmasthan (centre) kept open (traditional Vastu convention).

variants.label: Usability-first

entrance.note: No entrance was specified, so it was derived from plot.facing (E): E zone on the E wall. Send an `entrance` object to control it. A 2.4 unit foyer strip is held clear inside E so no room is packed against the door.
entrance.padaNote: The 32-pada perimeter grading is a separate computation — POST this bearingDeg with your plotPolygon and doorXY to /v2/astrology/vastu/entrance/pada. That scheme is later Vastu convention, not a classical verse, and is served verified:false there.
entrance.source: traditional Vastu convention (not a specific classical verse)

openings.note: Windows are placed on room walls that lie on the plot boundary; internal doors face the plot's circulation core. Sill 0.9 / head 2.1 (1.5 / 2.1 for service rooms) assume plot units are metres. These are a Vedika product default for visualisation, not a classical prescription — adjust them against your local building code.

thresholds.basis: fraction of the SAME wedge of the plot's bounding rectangle (the ideal regular plot). A mean-area baseline is not used: equal-angle wedges are unequal in area on any rectangle, so a mean baseline reports extensions and cuts on a flawless plot.
